title: Extent review
author: Fieldwork project
description: How far a set of points reaches, and whether that is large enough to look at. Draws the convex hull of the points, measures its area in a metric CRS, and classifies the hull against a stated threshold with the extent-review ruleset. The polygon comes out carrying its own status, so a map can colour it and anything downstream keeps the judgement.
mustNotBeReadAs: Not a judgement that a large area is a problem. Whether extent matters, and above what size, depends entirely on the question: a hull over 2 km2 is unremarkable for a city and alarming for a building footprint. The threshold is the practitioner’s to set and neither this composition nor the ruleset inside it ships a basis for any value. A hull is also an outline of what was OBSERVED, not a boundary anyone agreed to, and it encloses ground where nothing was recorded.

reviews.outcome: Assembled and executed, and substituted into the John Snow outbreak-extent example, which is how a composition is tested here. Not admitted to the palette: admission needs a human review and an ontology expansion, neither of which exists. Status stays private. Experiment 113.

parameters.name: threshold
parameters.title: Area above which to review, in square metres
